newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate lower, baht falls late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate lower, baht falls late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate eased slightly to 11.00-11.50 percent in late trade on Friday from 11.50 percent in the morning and late on Thursday, dealers said.
"We're not likely to see a further fall in the interbank rate next week. Heavy buying of the dollar today will certainly trigger some demand for funds next week," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The baht dipped to 25.500-25.510 to the dollar from 25.482-25.487 early and 25.477-25.482 late on Thursday on dollar's strength abroad, dealers said.
"The baht was weaker in line with dollar's sharp rise in the afternoon," said one currency dealer.
Dealers expect dollar buying to remain strong next week as some market players appeared to be relatively short of the dollar.
"Nobody wants to sell the dollar when the U.S. unit is expected to rise further," the dealer said.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was steady at 8.50/9.00 satangs per dollar against 8.00/9.00 in early morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate unchanged at 25.47.
